clue.text: Kind of ribbon used for decoration

definitions.meaning: a ... ribbon is the coloured strip from which a military award hangs
an honour pinned on a uniform for gallantry or service

explanation.definitionFit: One word names both the honour awarded for bravery and, attributively, the type of ribbon it hangs from.

parts.note: read plainly it is any manner of behaving; read theatrically it is the Stanislavski school of performance taken up by Brando

explanation.definitionFit: A way of doing anything is a procedure, and the Stanislavski-derived acting school bears the same name.

parts.note: prompt seems to mean quick, but it is the theatrical prompter feeding forgotten lines from the wings

explanation.walkthrough: 'prompt' looks like an adjective meaning swift; it is the stage prompt, given from the wings out of the audience's sight.
explanation.definitionFit: The prompter sits in the wings, out of the audience's view, beyond the acting area.

clue.text: Some err badly and show regret

indicators.note: done badly, the letters of the two words are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone who has made a few mistakes feels sorry about them.
explanation.definitionFit: Remorse is deep sorrow and guilt for a wrong committed, a strong synonym for regret.

clue.text: Little brothers tucked up in a bed, concentrating

indicators.note: tucked in, like children under covers, so one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: taken as written, the two words run together

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word for brothers is read from bottom to top

parts.note: bros is the shortened, little, form of brothers

explanation.surface: Small boys are put to bed while someone pays close attention.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' only makes sense in a down clue, where the brothers read from bottom to top; 'tucked' then puts them inside the bed, and 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone engrossed in a task is giving it full attention; both words describe rapt focus.

parts.note: Carrie is a girl's name
Don is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A romance begins, girl meets boy, with the story to be continued in the next episode.
explanation.definitionFit: To carry on is to keep going, so the past form means kept going or persisted.

parts.note: present in the sense of being in this place
after means coming behind, following

explanation.surface: A grammar lesson about tenses: present, then the one that follows, the future.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Present' suggests a tense or a gift; here it means in attendance.
explanation.definitionFit: The life to come, or time still ahead, is the noun sense of this word.

clue.text: A light abreast of the vessel

parts.note: a beam is a shaft of light

explanation.surface: A lamp shines out level with the side of a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A nautical term meaning at right angles to the ship's keel, level with its middle.
The word means both a round object and a grand formal evening of dancing.

clue.text: The Scot has his brief moment of masculine glory

parts.note: Mac is a familiar form of address for a Scotsman
mo is short for moment, as in half a mo

explanation.surface: A Scotsman enjoys his short spell of manly triumph.
explanation.definitionFit: Machismo is an exaggerated pride in manliness, a swaggering show of virility.

parts.note: looks like diplomacy, but means love affairs called by a French word

explanation.walkthrough: 'Foreign affairs' suggests diplomacy; it means romances with a French name.
explanation.definitionFit: The French word for loves, used in English for love affairs, often secret ones.

indicators.note: not quite the full word, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: ideal means perfect

explanation.surface: An idea that falls a little short of perfect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not quite' trims the last letter, L, from IDEAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A notion is a thought or concept that comes to mind.

parts.note: an old salt is a seasoned sailor
to beef is to complain

explanation.surface: A seaman complains about the cured rations aboard ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Brisket cured in brine, a deli staple, is meat kept edible by salting.

clue.text: Arm put round a pretty girl in game

indicators.note: the pretty girl is placed around the other pieces, enclosing them

parts.note: a belle is a beautiful woman
a gat is slang for a gun, a firearm

explanation.surface: Someone slips an arm around an attractive girl during a game.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface has the arm round the girl, but it is the girl who goes round. Bagatelle is a pub board game in which balls are struck into numbered holes.
explanation.definitionFit: A bagatelle is a board game played with balls and a cue, also a trifle.

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father
roles are the parts actors take

explanation.surface: Dad takes several acting parts in theatre productions.
explanation.definitionFit: A parole is a word of honour, a pledge, especially by a prisoner not to escape.

definitions.meaning: kept, as a festival or holiday is kept

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both remarked upon and kept, as a religious holiday is kept with ceremony.

clue.text: Fail to catch, or accidentally disclose

definitions.meaning: allow something to fall from the hands
reveal a secret without meaning to

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means allowing an object to fall and also mentioning something unintentionally.

clue.text: Sally in deep trouble when turned out

indicators.note: the witty remark goes inside the jumbled word
in trouble, the letters of the word are thrown into disorder

parts.note: a sally is a witty remark, a quip

explanation.surface: A girl called Sally is in deep difficulty when she is expelled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sally' looks like a name but is a witty remark; 'trouble' jumbles the second word, and 'in' sets the remark inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone well turned out is dressed and kitted for the occasion, fitted out.

indicators.note: the word for novel is placed in the setting provided by the word for authentic

parts.note: real means genuine, authentic
new means novel, fresh

explanation.surface: A literary history placing a novel among genuine Restoration works.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Restoration' suggests the period after 1660; here it means repair. 'novel' is not a book but an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Repairing or reviving something makes it fresh again, a restoring.

parts.note: pa's means father's
sable is the pelt of a small mammal prized for fur

explanation.surface: Father's fur coat is considered quite nice.
explanation.definitionFit: Passable means adequate, middling, as fair does in a modest verdict.

clue.text: The barrel end of a gun

definitions.meaning: a large cask for wine or beer
the thick end of a rifle held against the shoulder

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a large cask and the shoulder end of a rifle stock.
The noun means both habitual practices and the purposes to which something can be put.

indicators.note: making a new version of the word rearranges its letters

explanation.surface: A climber carries out a fresh climb up a mountain.
explanation.definitionFit: To enact is to act out or perform a play or a role.

clue.text: Time is not on our side

definitions.text: Time is not on our side

parts.words: Time is not on our side
parts.note: a familiar saying about running out of time, read literally as describing an opponent

explanation.definitionFit: The saying that time is against us names it as a foe, an adversary on the other side.

clue.text: There's no telling if this is to be kept

definitions.text: There's no telling if this is to be kept

parts.words: There's no telling if this is to be kept
parts.note: there's no telling seems to mean nobody knows; it means nobody may tell, if something is to stay confidential

explanation.walkthrough: 'There's no telling' reads as uncertainty; it means literally no telling anyone.
explanation.definitionFit: Something confidential stays hidden only while nobody tells it.

clue.text: Frank, ensnared in sex scandal, tells all

indicators.note: trapped inside, so one piece sits within the other
a scandal throws things into disarray, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: plain means frank, outspoken

explanation.surface: A man named Frank, caught up in a sex scandal, makes a full confession.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frank' looks like a name but is an adjective meaning outspoken; 'scandal' jumbles the three letters before 'ensnared in' traps the adjective among them.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who makes everything clear gives a full account, setting out every detail.

parts.note: looks like songs of the 1930s slump, but means melancholy music, depression meaning low spirits

explanation.walkthrough: 'the Depression' suggests the 1930s economic slump; the music is named after low spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: The African-American song form takes its name from a slang term for sadness.

clue.text: The impression it gives varies from day to day

definitions.text: The impression it gives varies from day to day

parts.words: The impression it gives varies from day to day
parts.note: impression seems to mean an opinion formed; it is an inked mark whose printed date changes each day

explanation.walkthrough: 'impression' suggests a feeling someone gives off; it is a literal inked stamp.
explanation.definitionFit: An office rubber stamp with adjustable numerals prints the current day on documents.
